newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Copper easing, but upside potential exists.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Copper easing, but upside potential exists.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Copper is weakening, but has a chance to spike higher on bullish fundamentals so long as $2,350 support holds, traders and analysts said on Wednesday.
Aluminium was likely to tread a narrowing range after Tuesday's gains. Although the upside was favoured, the market needed a convincing break above $1,660 for confirmation, they said.
COPPER - The market rebounded after drifting to a low of $2,346 per tonne on Tuesday's kerb, confirming strong support at $2,350.
Analysts said a break of $2,350 would lead the market down to $2,320, but a chance remained to spiral higher and re-challenge the key $2,400 resistance which failed on Monday.
"I don't think it's over yet," said one European trader, citing strong demand within Europe and the existence of uncovered shorts.

Copper's Bolinger bands were near the bottom end of the range at $2,350. This suggested that the market was consolidating, the trader said, adding, "We are going to see some kind of break out. I'm not sure in which direction yet."
A support line drawn from the April 18 low of $2,262 and through $2,275 and $2,287 indicated strong support at $2,350, he said.
But failure to hold that level might trigger stops expected around $2,340, pushing the market down to $2,320.
Martin Squires of Rudolf Wolff said technical indicators had yet to cross down. With stocks falling "we feel the market still has potential to spike higher". But a move to $2,320 was possible.
By 0730 GMT three month copper was indicated at $2,368/73 from Tuesday's close of $2,363/68. The cash-threes backwardation stood at a fairly steady $80/$90.

ALUMINIUM - The market secured its position above $1,600 further on Tuesday with gains extending to $1,638, but analysts said a consolidation could now be expected after prices failed to push above $1,640.
The European trader said a 50 percent retracement from the last move could take the market down to $1,625, where it would encounter strong support.
Aluminium's stochastics were "pretty overbought" at 91 percent, but a close above $1,640 could drag the market to $1,660.

Brokers Brandeis said the upside looked limited with good resistance at $1,640, and a move back to close the gap between $1,620 and $1,614 seemed more likely, unless good levels of consumer buying emerged.
By 0730 GMT three months aluminium was quoted at $1,641/43 a tonne compared with Tuesday's close of $1,638/40.
-- Clelia Oziel, London Newsroom +44-171-542 8071
